# Universal Credit taper and work allowance, in plain English

Figures: 2026-27. The rules this text is printed from are proved equal to the model's own definitions for every input and every parameter set (`ucTaperRule_eval`, `ucAward_eq_rule`); see [README.md](README.md) for what that does and does not cover.

## Universal Credit: the taper and the work allowance (UC Regulations 2013 reg 22)

To work out the amount your earnings take off your Universal Credit:

1. Start with your earned income for the month.
2. Take off your work allowance.
3. If that leaves less than £0, use £0.
4. Take 55% of that (the taper rate).

**Earned income** means your pay for the assessment period (a month) after income tax and National Insurance are taken off, together with your partner's if you claim as a couple.

**Work allowance** means the amount you can earn each month before Universal Credit starts to fall, if you are responsible for a child or have limited capability for work (see the table below). Other claimants have none, so all of their earned income counts.

| Your situation | Work allowance a month |
| --- | --- |
| Responsible for a child, or limited capability for work, and no housing costs in the award | £710 |
| Responsible for a child, or limited capability for work, with housing costs in the award | £427 |
| Anyone else | none (£0) |

Your Universal Credit for the month is your maximum amount (the standard allowance and any amounts for children, housing, childcare and so on), less any unearned income, less the amount worked out above. If that leaves less than £0, you get none.

For example, for a month, with the higher work allowance of £710:

| Earned income | The amount your earnings take off your Universal Credit |
| --- | --- |
| £300 | £0 |
| £710 | £0 |
| £1,000 | £159.50 |
| £2,000 | £709.50 |
| £3,000 | £1,259.50 |
